chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Kathīr, from his father, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام brought out Surāqah al-Hamdāniyyah, and the people nearly killed one another because of the crowding. When he saw that, he ordered that she be taken back until, when the crowding had lessened, she was brought out and the door was closed. He said: “So they pelted her until she died.” He said: Then he ordered regarding the door, and it was opened. He said: Then everyone who entered began cursing her. He said: When he saw that, he called out through his caller: “O people, withhold your tongues from her, for no hadd is carried out except that it is an expiation for that sin, just as a debt is discharged by a debt.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in the report
key_terms.الدَّيْنُ: Debt, used here in an analogy for discharge and settlement
key_terms.الذَّنْبِ: The sin for which the punishment was carried out
key_terms.الزِّحَامِ: Crowding or crush of people gathered at the event
key_terms.حَدٌّ: A legally prescribed punishment in Islamic law
key_terms.رَمَوْهَا: They pelted her as the carried-out punishment
key_terms.كَفَّارَةَ: An expiation that removes the burden of the sin
key_terms.يَلْعَنُهَا: They were cursing her after the punishment

ai.seo_question: Does the carrying out of a hadd punishment serve as expiation for the sin in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام supervised the execution of the hadd punishment in an orderly manner and prevented harm from the crowd. It also states that once the hadd had been carried out, the sin was expiated, so people were instructed not to continue reviling the woman.
